max_data_age_measured_from: the dekad label. 21 days of reader relevance past the window close, plus the 9 days from label to close.

boundary_notice.text: ASAP redrew its crop regions on 25 August 2026. Region counts on this page are not comparable with those published before 17 September.
boundary_notice.applies_until: region-level history on the new boundaries is long enough that the old one is no longer what a returning reader remembers; a season, not a week
boundary_notice.where: beside any count of regions, on the index and on every page that compares against an earlier dekad

methodology_changed.3.0: ASAP replaced its boundary layer, v05 to v06, on 2026-08-25 and switched its export to it (D-301). Every country id changed and 87 of 165 countries carry different regions: renamed, re-keyed, in many cases subdivided. Estonia is now 15 counties rather than one unit, Switzerland 25 cantons, France 13 regions rather than 22 on the post-2016 administrative map. Every region-level baseline for those countries is re-keyed, each new region against its own 26-year series from ASAP, so ranks remain like for like within a region but 'N of M regions' changes denominator for half the channel. regions_at_record_history restarts on v06. Nothing published before 2026-09-17 is comparable to what follows at the region level. Area weights come from gaul1_asap_v06; the crop calendar was not republished and stays keyed on v05 region ids, so region-level calendar joins do not resolve until ASAP reissues it.
methodology_changed.2.0: Country figures are area-weighted by ASAP's km2_crop (tls-internal#16). Previously an unweighted mean over regions, so England carried a quarter of the UK figure while holding 85.6% of its cropland. Affects every country value, and therefore severity, magnitude, rate and ranking_key. Ranks are computed on weighted values for EVERY year, so the comparison stays like for like. Regions with zero crop-mask area get no vote and the count is disclosed per place in `aggregate.regions_zero_area`.
methodology_changed.1.0: Unweighted mean over regions, launch to 2026-08-19.

instrument_order.means: shortest observation window first. An instrument that summarises one dekad moves sooner than one that integrates a season, so a fixed order shows which instruments CAN move first. That is a fact about the instruments and not about any event.
instrument_order.not: sorted by what moved. Never order these rows by observed movement: the ordering would then be a claim about sequence, and with `driver` unidentified in most places we cannot support one.

absence_reasons.no_current_value: the instrument has history here but no value for the dekad being reported, usually because it publishes behind the others
absence_reasons.undefined_at_this_dekad: the instrument is never defined for this region at this point in the season, which is seasonal rather than late
absence_reasons.too_few_comparable_years: fewer than 20 comparable years at this dekad
absence_reasons.not_published_for_country: ASAP does not publish this indicator for this country

chance_baseline_aggregate.measures: regions at their worst on record for this dekad, summed across reported places, per year
chance_baseline_aggregate._scope: reported places only, never the full catalogue. A baseline over a wider set than the page shows is not like-for-like and the discrepancy is invisible in the current year.

publication_cadence.window_days: 10, except the 21st which runs to month end

2026-07-21.basis: measured: window closed 31 July, first seen published 2026-08-09 by crops/probe_asap.py

2026-07-11.basis: UPPER BOUND, not a measurement: present in a cache pull dated 28 July, so published by then

age_days.means: the age of the newest observation CYCLES. It is at the floor the day a dekad publishes and grows by one each day until the next lands, roughly ten days later. Quoting the floor as the property is the error corrected in D-148.

publication_cadence._render: the CURRENT age must be computed at render from `dekad` against today, never stored. A stored age is wrong the day after it is written.

series_declaration.due_equals_expected_because: these series are indexed by year at one fixed dekad, so a slot is never pending. There is no NOT YET state in this channel's series.
series_declaration.applies_to: every `series` in this file, at country and region level. Each carries `series_span` with `present` and `missing`.
series_declaration.blindness: a slot that is present but is not a measurement is marked at the DATUM, not counted here. Instruments carry `absent` and `absent_because` across four states; places that never enter `places` carry a reason and an `ours` flag in `skipped`, which separates our own fetch failure from a fact about ASAP.
series_declaration.why: 24 values in a 26-year record and 24 values in a 24-year record are otherwise the same payload, so a renderer stretches what it has and turns a gap into an end.

baseline.unit: same dekad of each year, never a rolling window
baseline.means: every rank, percentile and z on this channel is computed against 25 prior observations, 2001-2025, at the SAME dekad. The current year is NOT in the baseline, so a z has no (n-1)/sqrt(n) ceiling. A rank of `N of 26` counts the 25 baseline years plus the current one.

rate_legend.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate_legend.applies_to: every `rate` block in this file, at country and region level alike
rate_legend.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

rate_legend._start_control_note: Every rate block carries `_start_control`. `holds` is true when the place is still rank 1 once the level it fell from is controlled for. NINE of the twenty rank-1 places on 2026-07-11 do not hold, so roughly half of rate-based leads are inflated by construction. `adjusted_rank` is a FITTED quantity and must never reach a reader: publish `start_value` and `start_rank`, which are measured. The underscore prefix marks the whole block as pipeline guidance that never renders.

raw.licensed_claim: NO SUPERLATIVE FROM THIS VARIANT AT ANY COUNT. It does not control for starting level or drift in the series, so a count that tops it is not a record, however large the margin, and prior_years_at_or_above being 0 here does not license one. Comparison only.

holding_the_control.licensed_claim: NO SUPERLATIVE FROM THIS VARIANT AT ANY COUNT. It does not control for drift in the series, so a count that tops it is not a record, however large the margin, and prior_years_at_or_above being 0 here does not license one. Comparison only.

time_detrended.licensed_claim: NO SUPERLATIVE FROM THIS VARIANT AT ANY COUNT. It does not control for starting level, so a count that tops it is not a record, however large the margin, and prior_years_at_or_above being 0 here does not license one. Comparison only.

both_controls.licensed_claim: Licensed: this many places are falling faster over 4 dekads than in any year of the record, after controlling for starting level and drift in the series.

rate_count_baseline._why: the raw count includes places whose steep fall is a fall from a high start, which is arithmetic rather than news; and the 4-dekad change carries an across-year trend, so a bare rank is partly drift. Both controls are needed and 13i measures why. Every variant carries superlative_survives_controls and licensed_claim because knowing WHICH figure to publish is not the same as knowing WHAT it licenses: on 2026-08-13 the correct variant was rendered and a record superlative shipped anyway, one control short.
rate_count_baseline._whole_set: this compares a COUNT against the history of the same count, so it needs no multiplicity correction. It does NOT establish any single country: rank 1 of 26 has p = 1/26, so a set this size produces about four by chance.

global.buckets_do_not_partition: crop_outcome and meteorology are named groups, not a partition: Vegetation, current and Water satisfaction belong to neither. A page claiming the two diverged has to show what went into each.

qualifiers.text: Detrending moves these two figures in opposite directions, so raw and detrended are both emitted and neither stands alone. Temperature worsens almost everywhere and cropland greens, so the raw gap between them is widened by two secular trends rather than by this season alone.
0.5 is the mean of every place's own series by construction and is not a normal to compare against. Use the observed range across the record, which is what the series carries.

The crop outcome instrument is cumulative over the growing cycle, so at this dekad it integrates a season that has not finished. It is a reading of conditions to date and carries no statement about the rest of the season.

method_short: FPAR cumulated z-score, ASAP crop mask, growing cycle only
method: FPAR cumulated z-score, ASAP crop mask, restricted to the growing cycle. The indicator is cumulative over the season, so one dekad encodes the season to date.

instrument_disagreement._what: regions where the fast vegetation instrument is at its own record low while a water instrument sits in its own best third, at this dekad

definition.vegetation_at_record: `zfpar`, current vegetation, at rank 1 of its own 26 years at this dekad
definition.water_favourable: `wsi` OR `spi3` at a rank in the best third of its own 26 years, that is rank > 2/3 of the years available
definition.population: every published region carrying a current-vegetation reading at this dekad

instrument_disagreement.statement: 41 of the 381 regions at a record low on current vegetation have water or rainfall sitting in its own best third at the same moment, about one in nine
instrument_disagreement.is_not: a share of all regions. It is a share of those ALREADY at a vegetation record. Of every region we measure, the figure is `share_of_all`, which is much smaller. A sentence that says 'across the regions on this site' and then quotes `share_of_record` overstates it by an order of magnitude, which is the error this field replaced.

isthmus_comparison._what: the Central American isthmus, each country against its own 26 years of the composite
isthmus_comparison.geography_is_declared: the member list and its order are stated, not derived. Only membership of the worst-k band is computed.
isthmus_comparison.statement: 7 of the 8 countries of the isthmus are in their own worst four of 26 years. 3 of the 8 were worse in 2015 than they are now.
isthmus_comparison.is_not: evidence about any earlier dekad or any earlier boundary layer. Every count here is 2026 against its own 26 years on the current boundaries. On depth: a prior year matches or beats this one at 4 of 6 thresholds (worst-3: 2015; worst-4: 2015; worst-5: 2015; worst-6: 2015), and at none of worst-1, worst-2, so the count DOES depend on where the cut is drawn. Read counts_now beside prior_years_at_or_above rather than the headline count alone. A tie with a prior year counts AS at record (see ties_count_as_at_record and at_record_tied). Publish `statement`.

country_record_baseline._what: countries with at least one crop region at its own worst on record for this point in the season, per year
country_record_baseline.statement: 65 countries have at least one crop region at its own worst on record. The prior 25 years range from 24 to 91 with a mean of 36.6, so this is the 2th highest of 26 and an ordinary reading.
country_record_baseline.is_not: an alarm on its own. This count is ordinary in most years and the range is wide. Do not publish the figure without `prior_mean` or `rank_among_years` beside it. `even_spread` is NOT an expectation to test against: records cluster within a country, so the observed count sits below it in most years without that meaning a calm season.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 18 regions counts equally, so one carries 6% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.259, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 28 regions counts equally, so one carries 4% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.238, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 1st steepest fall of 26
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 22nd highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time

severity.statement: The most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 17 regions counts equally, so one carries 6% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.213, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 14 regions counts equally, so one carries 7% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The 14th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.212, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: rose over this window, ranking 24th of 26 by fall steepness, from the 25th highest starting level of those 26
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: A rise, ranking 24th of 26 by fall steepness over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 25th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 14 regions counts equally, so one carries 7% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.168, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 1st steepest fall of 26
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 25th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 4 regions counts equally, so one carries 25% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.257, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 1st steepest fall of 26
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 21st highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 2nd lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 20 regions counts equally, so one carries 5% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.203, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 2nd lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 45 regions counts equally, so one carries 2% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.244, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 1st steepest fall of 26
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 8th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 2nd lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 9 regions counts equally, so one carries 11% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The 13th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.229, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 12th steepest fall of 26, but from the 24th highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 12th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 24th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 2nd lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 29 regions counts equally, so one carries 3% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.215, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 4th steepest fall of 26, but from the 21st highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 4th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 21st highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 3rd lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 18 regions counts equally, so one carries 6% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The 11th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.208, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: rose over this window, ranking 15th of 26 by fall steepness, from the 24th highest starting level of those 26
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: A rise, ranking 15th of 26 by fall steepness over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 24th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 3 regions counts equally, so one carries 33% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The joint 2nd most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together, level with 2010
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 4th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 25 regions counts equally, so one carries 4% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The joint most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together, level with 2024
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.191, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 7th steepest fall of 26, but from the 16th highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 7th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 16th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 6th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 22 regions counts equally, so one carries 5% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The 12th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.15, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 2nd steepest fall of 26
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 2nd steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 6th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 6th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 21 regions counts equally, so one carries 5% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The 2nd most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.203, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 13th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 7th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 9 regions counts equally, so one carries 11% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.243, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.
