chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 7th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 5 regions counts equally, so one carries 20% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The 2nd most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.217, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 8th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 1 regions counts equally, so one carries 100% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.179, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 10th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 20th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 8th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 1 regions counts equally, so one carries 100% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The joint 6th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together, level with 2003
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 9th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 13 regions counts equally, so one carries 8% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The 3rd most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.244, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 3rd steepest fall of 26, but from the 11th highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 3rd steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 11th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 9th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 34 regions counts equally, so one carries 3% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.198, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: rose over this window, ranking 12th of 26 by fall steepness, from the 18th highest starting level of those 26
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: A rise, ranking 12th of 26 by fall steepness over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 18th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 9th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 17 regions counts equally, so one carries 6% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The 3rd most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.13, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: rose over this window, ranking 23rd of 26 by fall steepness, from the 20th highest starting level of those 26
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: A rise, ranking 23rd of 26 by fall steepness over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 20th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 11th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 8 regions counts equally, so one carries 12% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The joint 12th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together, level with 2009
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.105, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 5th steepest fall of 26, but from the 14th highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 5th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 14th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 12th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 42 regions counts equally, so one carries 2% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The 2nd most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.184, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 1st steepest fall of 26, but from the 9th highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 9th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 13th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 10 regions counts equally, so one carries 10% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 13th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 19 regions counts equally, so one carries 5% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The 2nd most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.161, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: rose over this window, ranking 26th of 26 by fall steepness, from the 24th highest starting level of those 26
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: A rise, ranking 26th of 26 by fall steepness over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 24th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 15th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 19 regions counts equally, so one carries 5% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The 9th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.235, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 6th steepest fall of 26, but from the 7th highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 6th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 7th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 15th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 17 regions counts equally, so one carries 6% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.085, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 15th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 23 regions counts equally, so one carries 4% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The joint 6th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together, level with 2013
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.214, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: rose over this window, ranking 14th of 26 by fall steepness, from the 14th highest starting level of those 26
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: A joint rise, ranking 14th of 26 by fall steepness over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, level with 2022, from the 14th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 16th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 26 regions counts equally, so one carries 4% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The joint 6th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together, level with 2019
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.14, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 10th steepest fall of 26, but from the 10th highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 10th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 10th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 16th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 10 regions counts equally, so one carries 10% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The 14th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.164, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 5th steepest fall of 26, but from the 8th highest starting level of those 26, so it is not a record fall once that is accounted for
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 5th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 8th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 16 regions counts equally, so one carries 6% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
Vegetation and the water instruments do not co-vary here, so this stress cannot be described as water-driven. The reading is the condition only.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 16th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 21 regions counts equally, so one carries 5% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.153, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 2nd steepest fall of 26
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 2nd steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 7th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 17th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 13 regions counts equally, so one carries 8% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The 25th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.174, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: rose over this window, ranking 19th of 26 by fall steepness, from the 15th highest starting level of those 26
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: A rise, ranking 19th of 26 by fall steepness over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 15th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time

severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

chance_baseline.measures: admin units at their worst on record for this dekad, per year
chance_baseline._note: uniform_would_say is shown only to be argued with. Use recent_mean.
chance_baseline._order_by: filter on selected_for_display, order by excess_share. Never order on clears_own_recent_max alone: it is a boolean over a small sample and puts 1-against-0 beside 8-against-3. And the COUNT of selected places is not a finding: it sits at the 57th percentile of the last 35 dekads.

qualifiers.text: ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.

magnitude.is_not: the composite. This is the crop-outcome instrument's LEVEL alone, and it is the slowest of the six. For how stressed a place is across all reporting instruments use `severity.rank`; for how fast it is deteriorating use `rate`.
magnitude.statement: 17th lowest of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026

ranking_key.excludes: Vegetation, cumulative, by product's ruling: it integrates from sowing so it cannot say what is abnormal NOW. Still published as the outcome measure.
ranking_key.method: mean position of each region-instrument reading within its own 2001-2025 history at this dekad, 1.0 = worst on record. Derived from the published ranks so it cannot drift from them.
ranking_key.is_not: a COUNT, and not the same aggregation as `severity`. It IS an intensity: the cropland-weighted mean of how far each region sits into its own history, so a choropleth of it reads correctly. It differs from `severity` in aggregation order, averaging region-level positions and weighting them by cropland where severity averages instrument positions of the country-level values. For a count of regions at their record use `share_at_record`; for how fast conditions are moving, use `rate`.

aggregate.method: unweighted mean across regions: the cropland reference data was not present at build time
aggregate.caveat: each of the 5 regions counts equally, so one carries 20% of this figure whatever its cropland area: the cropland reference data was absent at build time, so this figure is NOT area-weighted

severity.statement: The joint 12th most stressed of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, across 5 instruments read together, level with 2015
severity.is_not: a cross-place ordering. The value places a country against ITSELF, and the rank saturates: 37 of the 165 published countries, about one in four, sit at rank 1, so sorting on it yields a large tied block broken by payload order. For how much of a country is abnormal, use `regions_at_record`, which is a proportion and therefore comparable between places. For how fast, use `rate`.
severity.method: Each of 5 instruments placed within its own 25 prior years at this dekad, then averaged with equal weights. No instrument is weighted above another.

qualifiers.text: Every input is measured against its own record, but no source publishes this average. It is our combination, not an observation.

This value places the country against itself, so it does not rank countries against each other. Its year-to-year spread here is 0.146, and that spread differs by place, so a higher value elsewhere can be a less unusual year than this one. The rank is the comparable figure.
A reading of conditions to date. It carries no statement about the rest of the season.

rate.licensed_claim: 7th steepest fall of 26
rate.start_means: the level this fall began from, ranked 1 = highest on record. A steep fall from a high start is partly regression toward the mean.
rate.statement: The 7th steepest fall over 4 dekads of 26 observations for this point in the season, 2001-2026, from the 9th highest starting level of those 26
rate.measures: change in cumulative FPAR z-score over the 4 dekads ending at the reported one
rate.method: Cumulative FPAR z-score now minus the same indicator 4 dekads earlier, ranked against the same window in each prior year. A rate of change, not a level: a place can be ordinary and falling faster than in any year on record.

qualifiers.text: This ranks how fast the reading is moving, not how bad it is. A steep fall from a good starting point can still leave a place in ordinary condition, and the level field says which.
ASAP observes the crop canopy, not what stressed it. Heat, drought, disease and late planting are not separable in this measurement.
